Maria (oncall): Quick sync from the post-incident runbook review — SFO region experienced prolonged degraded GPU capacity during yesterday's surge, and the traffic-shift cooldowns were too short which caused oscillation when we tried to move slices. TL;DR: need runbook + automation fixes.
Chen (infra): Agree. Root cause was twofold: one network spine flap that reduced pod churn tolerance, and the autoscaler thresholds for thin pool reserves were too aggressive.
Raj (sre): Notes from the blameless review: we triggered a slice shift at 12:03, then immediately rebalanced back at 12:07 because the health checks bounced. That in turn kept requeuing pods and exhausted the warm pool.
Priya (eng-runtime): We should add a debounce on policy-driven shifts and ensure a minimum steady-state window (suggest 10m) before reversing. Also the KV cache warmup penalty is higher than we estimated.
Alex (prodops): Actionable runbook items I propose: 1) Increase shift cooldown to 600s, 2) Add a manual gating step for >50% traffic shifts during peak hours, 3) Autoscaler fallback to reserve 10% thin-pool for 30m after large shifts.
Nora (docs): I'll draft the runbook edits once we agree on wording. Will add a 'when to abort and when to escalate' checklist and a quick troubleshooting commands section.
Maria (oncall): ops-bot, please add a ticket for runbook + automation changes and assign to Chen/Raj/Priya.
ops-bot: Created ISSUE-2987: "SFO failover cooldowns & thin-pool reserve adjustments" assigned to Chen, Raj, Priya. Link: https://ourtracker/ISSUE-2987 :white_check_mark:
Chen (infra): Implementation plan: I'll change the traffic shift controller default cooldown param to 600s and add a hysteresis flag so we only allow reversal after 600s + 2 successful health-check windows. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/432 (wip).
Priya (eng-runtime): I'll add a runtime metric to expose KV-cache hit-rate during slice shifts so SLOs can detect warmup regressions. Plan to instrument and then wire to Optimize suggestions. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/221
Raj (sre): For autoscaler: I'll add a reserve policy that keeps 10% GPUs in a warm state for 30m after a large shift (>30% traffic). Also adding alert if warm pool drops below soft-threshold for more than 5m.
Alex (prodops): Cost note — reserved warm pool means ~+$12k/month for SFO baseline. We should add that to the runbook as a tradeoff and a finance-approved knob.
Maria (oncall): Escalation flow: if shift fails twice in 30m, escalate to Eng-Infra + SRE + ProdOps on-call. Add step to rollback to previous slice weights and open a post-incident ticket.
Nora (docs): Draft PR for runbook edits will include the escalation flow, commands, and the cost appendix. I'll open docs PR once ISSUE-2987 has assigned owners.
Priya (eng-runtime): Quick troubleshooting snippet for oncall to paste into the runbook:
```
# check slice health
kubectl -n redwood get pods -l slice=sfo -o wide
# check warm pool
./tools/warmpool status --region sfo
# force drain with timeout
./tools/traffic-shift apply --from sfo --to ams --pct 30 --timeout 15m
```
Raj (sre): Also add a note: prefer staged shifts (10% -> 30% -> 50%) during peak to avoid warmup cliffs.
Chen (infra): Timeline: I can have the controller param change + unit tests by EOD Thu. Priya and Raj aim to have metric + autoscaler changes in next sprint.
Maria (oncall): Owners: Chen (controller), Priya (runtime metrics), Raj (autoscaler + alerts), Nora (docs). Ops-bot update please.
ops-bot: ISSUE-2987 updated with owners and tasks. Linked PRs: ops#432, runtime#221.
Alex (prodops): Can we schedule a 30m runbook review session tomorrow 10:00 PT to sign-off docs + knobs?
Nora (docs): I can do 10:00 PT, will send calendar invite and include checklist and diff preview.
Maria (oncall): Thanks team — please add any additional minor actions here. I'll close the loop once PRs are merged and we run one dry-run traffic shift in staging. :thumbsup:
